$comment: Every column a CLIENT PORTAL CONTACT can read from a base table, with why.
RLS filters rows, not columns, and Supabase has one `authenticated` role --
so any column on a table a contact has row access to is visible to them.
Checked by `npm run check:portal-exposure`. A new column fails the check
until it is either moved to a staff-only side table or listed here with a
reason. See README, 'Row-shaped vs field-shaped sensitivity'.

approvals.why_readable: Their own decision on a quote -- the record of what they agreed to.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.note: The note they themselves wrote when deciding.
columns.snapshot: What they were shown when they approved, built by app.quote_snapshot(), which selects only client-facing fields.

clients.why_readable: Their own client record -- the account the portal is showing them.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.name: Their own name.
columns.external_ref: Their own reference in the contractor's system; shown on documents anyway.
columns.archived_at: Whether their own account is archived.
columns.created_by: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque staff uuid, same criterion as lead_tech_id.

invoice_line_items.why_readable: The lines of an invoice issued to them; hidden while the invoice is a draft.

columns.position: Line order on their own invoice.
columns.kind: Line type on their own invoice.
columns.catalog_item_id: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque uuid into the contractor's catalogue; carries no price or name on its own.
columns.description: What they are being charged for.
columns.unit: Unit on their own invoice line.
columns.quantity: Quantity they are being charged for.
columns.unit_price_cents: The rate they are being charged.
columns.tax_rate: Tax rate applied to their line.

invoices.why_readable: An invoice issued to them. Drafts are excluded by the policy -- a draft is staff working out what to charge.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.number: The invoice number they will pay against.
columns.status: Whether their invoice is outstanding, paid or void. Drafts are excluded by the policy.
columns.notes: Client-facing notes, copied from the quote. There is deliberately NO internal note column on this table -- per the standard it would belong in invoice_internal_notes.
columns.issued_at: When the invoice was issued to them.
columns.voided_at: When the invoice was cancelled -- useful to them, not hidden from them.
columns.payment_ref: The reference the office recorded for their payment, so they can match it to their own bank. Hiding it generates "we already paid that" calls.
columns.created_by: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque staff uuid, same criterion as jobs.lead_tech_id -- no name, no email, no amount.

job_evidence.why_readable: Photos and notes a dispatcher chose to share (client_visible), on a non-draft job.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.storage_path: Needed to sign a URL for the photo they are allowed to see.
columns.mime_type: Type of a photo they can see.
columns.byte_size: Size of a photo they can already download.
columns.width: Dimensions of a photo they can see.
columns.height: Dimensions of a photo they can see.
columns.caption: The caption -- only on rows marked client_visible.
columns.body: The note text -- only on rows marked client_visible.
columns.client_visible: Always true for any row they can read, so it reveals nothing.
columns.captured_at: When the photo or note was taken.
columns.captured_by: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque staff uuid, same criterion as lead_tech_id. A client sees that someone took the photo, not who.
columns.client_ref: The uploader's idempotency key. An opaque uuid.

jobs.why_readable: The client requested this job and must be able to see it. Draft jobs are excluded by the policy.

columns.org_id: The contractor they are dealing with; already known from the portal URL.
columns.number: The reference they quote on the phone.
columns.title: Their own job title.
columns.status: The state of their own job or quote.
columns.requested_by_contact_id: Their own contact who raised the request.
columns.lead_tech_id: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: an opaque staff uuid with no name or email attached. The client learns that someone is assigned and nothing else. Left on `jobs` because the list renders it and jobs_tech_update keys off it; moving it would contort the assignment model to hide almost nothing.
columns.scheduled_end: When work is booked to finish.
columns.created_by: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque staff uuid, same criterion as lead_tech_id.

quote_line_items.why_readable: The lines of a quote sent to them; hidden while the parent quote is a draft.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.position: Line order on their own quote.
columns.catalog_item_id: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque uuid into the contractor's catalogue. Carries no price, name or description on its own.
columns.unit: Unit on their own quote line.
columns.quantity: Quantity on their own quote line.

quotes.why_readable: A quote sent to them. Drafts are excluded by the policy.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.number: The reference they quote on the phone.
columns.status: The state of their own job or quote.
columns.notes: Client-facing notes on the quote. The staff-only note lives in quote_internal_notes.
columns.sent_at: When the quote was sent to them.
columns.locked_at: When the quote was frozen for sending. A timestamp about their own document.

sites.why_readable: Their own sites, so a request can name one.

columns.org_id: The contractor; already known from the portal URL.
columns.name: Their own name.
columns.timezone: Their own site timezone, used to render dates correctly.
columns.archived_at: Whether their own site is archived.

organizations.why_readable: The contractor whose portal they are looking at. organizations_portal_select (app.portal_orgs()) hands a contact the org row so the portal shell can render a name and branding from the URL slug. This table was invisible to this check until the predicate was widened to match the whole app.portal_* family -- it was the only portal-readable table using an accessor other than portal_clients().

columns.id: The contractor's id; already on every row they can read.
columns.slug: In the URL they are looking at.
columns.name: The contractor's name -- the point of the policy.
columns.logo_path: Branding, rendered in the portal shell.
columns.brand_color: Branding, rendered in the portal shell.
columns.timezone: Renders their own job dates in the contractor's zone.
columns.currency: Formats their own quote and invoice amounts.
columns.default_tax_rate: REVIEW: the contractor's DEFAULT tax rate, shown nowhere in the portal. The rate that applied to them is already on their own quote and invoice lines. Here by accident of the row, not by decision.
columns.invoice_prefix: REVIEW: appears on their own invoice numbers anyway, so the exposure is nil -- but it was never signed off.
columns.invoice_terms_days: REVIEW: the contractor's DEFAULT payment terms. Their own invoice already carries its own due date.
columns.created_at: When the contractor's account was created.
columns.created_by: ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: opaque staff uuid, same criterion as clients.created_by.
